land.text: Tailevu and Naitasiri (with Bau island) and Lomaiviti, the Kubuna provinces of the Kubuna page read back into the 1850s-60s: a 35 km circle at 178.45 E, 17.75 S for Tailevu and Naitasiri (10 land cells, about 2,530 km2 at the grid, against 955 km2 for Tailevu and 1,666 km2 for Naitasiri on their pages) and a 60 km circle at 179.1 E, 17.75 S for Lomaiviti (Ovalau, Gau, Koro, Nairai). Natural Earth's Central Division is not used: it also holds Rewa, Namosi and Serua

successors.note: June 1871: Cakobau, Vunivalu of Bau, becomes Tui Viti (King of Fiji); Bau and its Kubuna lands are the core of the Kingdom of Fiji.

capitals.name: Bau (island, Tailevu)
capitals.note: Kubuna page: 'Capital: Bau island, Tailevu'. The Cakobau page says he 'established' Levuka 'as his capital' without a date; Levuka is the capital of the Kingdom of Fiji from 1871. Coordinates approximate; no page opened gives them.

rulers.name: Seru Epenisa Cakobau
rulers.title: Vunivalu of Bau (1852); Chairman of the Viti Confederacy 1865-1867; Tui Bau (King of Bau) 1867-1869
rulers.note: 'On 8 December 1852, Cakobau succeeded as Vunivalu of Bau'; infobox: Chairman 8 May 1865 - 2 May 1867, Tui Bau 2 May 1867 - 1869. The page does not say what he was called in 1869-1871; Tui Viti from 5 June 1871.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Bau row). Corrected after review: the first draft drew Natural Earth's Central Division, which besides Tailevu and Naitasiri holds Rewa, Namosi and Serua, the Burebasaga side (Rewa Province page: Rewa 'is the hinterland of the national capital and the heart of the Burebasaga Confederacy'), so the draft gave Bau its rival's land. The Kubuna page lists the confederacy's provinces (Tailevu, Naitasiri, Lomaiviti, Ra, Rotuma, parts of Ba) and 'the chiefly island of Bau in Tailevu'; the Tailevu Province page: 'Bau District includes Bau Island, the seat of the Kubuna Confederacy'. Tailevu and Naitasiri are now a 35 km circle at 178.45 E, 17.75 S, whose 10 land cells (about 2,530 km2) match the two provinces' areas together (955 km2 for Tailevu, whose body text says 755, and 1,666 km2 for Naitasiri: 2,621 km2); its south edge takes in Nausori, which the Tailevu page calls Tailevu's main town, and leaves out Suva, Namosi and Serua. Lomaiviti stays the 60 km circle at 179.1 E (2 land cells, about 506 km2). No page dates this extent to the 1850s-60s, so it is a confidence-1 reading. The Cakobau page says only that he claimed 'Bau had suzerainty over the remainder of Fiji'; that claim is not drawn. Ra, parts of Ba (Western Division) and Rotuma are left out. No page gives an area.

ledger.note: 1852: Cakobau becomes Vunivalu of Bau. 'On 8 December 1852, Cakobau succeeded as Vunivalu of Bau.' The Bau Island page says Bau 'became Fiji's dominant power' by the mid-1800s ('By the 1850s Bau dominated western Fiji', which cannot be right for an island off the east coast of Viti Levu) and dates an earlier Vunivalu, Naulivou, to 1791. The dossier starts at the first date the pages give for Cakobau's rule; the land is the researcher's reading. Land corrected after review (2026-10-18): Tailevu, Naitasiri and Lomaiviti only, not the Central Division (see keyframe 0).

1867: Cakobau becomes Tui Bau, King of Bau. Cakobau page infobox: 'Tui Bau (King of Bau) 2 May 1867 - 1869', after 'Chairman, Viti Confederacy 8 May 1865 - 2 May 1867' ('On 8 May 1865, a Confederacy of Independent Kingdoms of Viti was established'); the confederacy is an association and is not drawn as territory.

ledger.note: 1871: Bau becomes the core of the Kingdom of Fiji. 'he finally succeeded in creating a united Fijian kingdom in 1871'; infobox 'Tui Viti (King of Fiji) 5 June 1871 - 10 October 1874'; the Bau Island page: 'was able to unite all of Fiji's disparate tribes under his authority in 1871'. The land handed over is the corrected Tailevu, Naitasiri and Lomaiviti stand-in, the same as kingdom-of-fiji's predecessor land.

wars.name: Battle of Kaba
wars.outcome: Cakobau, aided by the King of Tonga, defeated the rebel chiefs; no land is recorded as changing hands.
wars.note: George Tupou I page: 'Tupou defeated Cakobau's enemies at the Battle of Kaba in 1855.' Cakobau page (no year): 'The last, brief rebellion of chiefs against Cakobau's rule culminated in the Battle of Kaba' and 'Cakobau crushed the rebellion with the aid of the King of Tonga.' Neither page names Rewa or gives a place for Kaba; the belligerent string 'Rewa and the Bauan rebels' is the one kingdom-of-tonga's /wars/0 uses (its 'Battle of Kaba' is the same battle) and rests on that dossier, not on a page opened here.

certainty.note: A chiefdom's sphere, not a surveyed territory; the page dates no conquest. Island coasts are exact.

sources.title: Seru Epenisa Cakobau
sources.note: Vunivalu 8 December 1852; Viti Confederacy 1865-1867; Tui Bau 1867-1869; Tui Viti 5 June 1871; the Battle of Kaba (undated).

sources.title: Bau Island
sources.note: Thin page: Naulivou 1791, Bau's rise by the 1850s, Cakobau's 1854 conversion, unification in 1871; no wars, no coordinates.

sources.title: Kubuna
sources.note: Provinces of the Kubuna confederacy and its capital Bau island; no historical dates before 1989.

sources.title: Enele Maʻafu
sources.note: Cakobau's 1858 offer to cede Fiji; Ma'afu's Tovata; used for the Tovata dossier and the relation of the two.

sources.title: George Tupou I
sources.note: Battle of Kaba 'in 1855' won by Tupou for Cakobau; Tupou met Cakobau in 1853; Maʻafu conquered Vanua Balavu 1854; Tonga's claims to Fiji ended 1869. Rewa is not mentioned.

sources.title: Tailevu Province
sources.note: Area 955 km2 (infobox; body text 755); main town Nausori on the Rewa River; Bau District includes Bau Island, the seat of the Kubuna Confederacy. No dated history.

sources.title: Naitasiri Province
sources.note: Area 1,666 km2; provincial centre Vunidawa; adjoins Rewa Province. No coordinates, no 1850s-60s history.

sources.title: Rewa Province
sources.note: Area 272 km2, includes Suva; 'the heart of the Burebasaga Confederacy'. Silent on the Bau-Rewa wars and on Rewa's extent.

sources.title: Ratu Tanoa Visawaqa
sources.note: Tried for the Bau-Rewa wars: silent on Rewa and Verata; confirms Cakobau inherited the Vunivalu title on his father's death in 1852.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks; the Fiji dossier (kingdom-of-fiji) names it as a predecessor. 'Kingdom of Bau' did not load as a Wikipedia title (URL_NOT_FOUND); the Bau Island page is the article, and the three pages that carry dates are thin. Start 1852 is the first page-dated year of Cakobau's rule, not the origin of Bau's paramountcy (the Bau Island page: Naulivou installed Vunivalu in 1791; the island 'then called Bau in 1760', which the page itself treats as inconsistent). Not on any page opened: the Bau-Rewa wars and their dates (Rewa, Verata, Kaba), the Battle of Kaba (the Cakobau page says only that it ended 'the last, brief rebellion of chiefs against Cakobau's rule'), Cakobau's 1858 and 1862 offers to cede Fiji (Ma'afu page: first offer 1858; Britain's decision not to annex 1862), the Confederacy of Independent Kingdoms of Viti's members (it is an association, type umbrella, 8 May 1865 to 2 May 1867, not drawn), the 1869-1871 title of Cakobau, the extent of Bau's real control in the interior (the Kai Colo). The Burebasaga confederacy (Rewa, Kadavu, the south and west) has no dossier and no page opened dates it: counterparts_needing_dossiers. Region names: Tailevu and Naitasiri are a 35 km radius at 178.45 E, 17.75 S and Lomaiviti a 60 km radius at 179.1 E, 17.75 S (gazetteer_names_needed: Tailevu, Naitasiri, Lomaiviti, Bau place). Review repair of 2026-10-18: (1) the Central Division is replaced everywhere (keyframe, found, dissolve, successor land) by the Tailevu and Naitasiri circle plus the Lomaiviti circle; the exclusion of Rewa, Namosi and Serua rests on the Kubuna page's list of provinces and the Rewa Province page ('the heart of the Burebasaga Confederacy'), not on any page about the Bau-Rewa wars. (2) Battle of Kaba added to wars (1855, zones empty). The Cakobau page gives no year for it and neither it nor the George Tupou I page names Rewa; the Rewa string is kept to match kingdom-of-tonga. (3) Still on no page opened: the Bau-Rewa wars, Bau's real extent in 1852-1871, Cakobau's title in 1869-1871. Ratu Tanoa Visawaqa, Rewa Province, Tailevu Province and Naitasiri Province were opened for them and are silent (only the 1852 succession and the provinces' areas).
